## Why
When the completion verifier fails a close with "insufficient evidence" because the evidence search EXHAUSTED its step budget without refuting any criterion, the correct next action is mechanical: run it again. The verdict cache (Gerrit 1796) banks per-criterion PASSes at finalize even on overall FAIL, so a re-run seeds the credited criteria and spends its whole budget on the formerly-insufficient ones. This was demonstrated live (2026-08-14, ticket deadbeat-warlike-ostrich / 8d74): first close FAILed on exhaustion; an identical re-run closed clean with zero operator-added evidence. Operator ruling: bounded-search exhaustion is the gate's problem to resolve, not the operator's — the gate should auto-resume instead of demanding a human retype the same command.

## Mechanism (maps to existing callables only)
A resumption is a WHOLE-VERIFIER RE-RUN — exactly what the manual 8d74 re-close did — not a partial continuation. No new verification entry point:
1. The resumption loop lives at the shared close-gate verification seam: `close_precheck._completion_precheck` (src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:497), specifically wrapping its `llm.verify_completion(...)` invocation (:638) and the verdict inspection that follows. This IS the shared seam — CLI, MCP, and library closes all flow through `rebar.transition` -> transition.py:23 -> `transition_close.close_ticket` (:454 calls `_completion_precheck`) -> that one call site. `gate_dispatch.produce_completion_verdict` / `CompletionAgentStep` are verdict PRODUCERS inside `verify_completion` and are NOT touched.
2. Classification: a FAIL qualifies for auto-resume ONLY when it is insufficiency-only. The framework ALREADY computes exactly this: `_insufficiency_only(result)` (src/rebar/llm/completion_reconcile.py:115) is True when every unmet criterion carries the framework-derived `evidence_sufficient: false` marker (set by the banking/assembly seams; reconcile derives and strips model-minted markers at :198-210, so a model cannot mint it) and at least one unmet record exists; an unmet record WITHOUT the marker is a genuine refutation → no resume. This ticket REUSES that predicate unchanged — no new schema field, no model-facing vocabulary, no prompt change. Existing consumers of the signal (completion_reconcile derivation :198, `_insufficiency_only` :115, completion_sidecar payload passthrough :382, completion_tool_policy, the finalizer prompt's banked-evidence rule) are enumerated in the change and stay untouched; the resumption loop is a NEW caller of the existing predicate.
3. On qualification: re-invoke `verify_completion` with the same args/ref. The verdict cache seeds credited PASSes (existing behavior, no change needed); the fresh budget concentrates on remaining criteria (budget derivation unchanged — `verify_step_floor` stays parameterized on the total criteria count; concentration is emergent from cache hits consuming ~0 steps, as observed in the 8d74 live run).
4. Bounded by count AND by progress. Count: `verify.auto_resume_max` resumptions per close invocation, default 2, 0 disables. Progress: a resumption is only dispatched when the just-finished attempt made progress — its cache-credited PASS count strictly exceeds the attempt before it (the first FAIL's credited count is the baseline). A zero-progress attempt means the next re-run would be an identical spin (same seeded cache, same budget, same remainder), so the loop stops early and surfaces the failure even with resumptions remaining. Each attempt logged to the ticket trail (comment or verdict metadata): attempt number, criteria credited-from-cache count, criteria remaining.
5. Overall outcome: PASS on any attempt → close proceeds. Still exhausted after the bounded resumptions → the existing failure surface, with the message stating auto-resume was attempted N times (operator sees honest state).

## Out of scope (split to child idea ticket)
Search-frontier handoff (steering a resumption away from already-searched places / toward where credited evidence was found) requires an argument-level tool-call transcript the verifier telemetry does not currently carry. That capability question — and the extractor design on top of it — is a separate idea ticket linked discovered_from this one; THIS ticket's resumption passes no frontier and needs no fallback (cache seeding alone proved sufficient live).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Qualification is `_insufficiency_only` (completion_reconcile.py:115) REUSED — asserted by test that the resumption loop calls it (no parallel reimplementation); no schema/prompt changes (diff-scope test or review assertion).
- [ ] Auto-resume triggers only on insufficiency-only FAILs: unit tests cover (a) all-unmet carry evidence_sufficient:false → resumes; (b) any unmet without the marker (refutation) → fails fast, no resume; (c) plain PASS → no resume; (d) FAIL with zero unmet records → no resume.
- [ ] Resumption re-invokes the existing `verify_completion` entry (asserted via call-count on the real seam), with the same ref binding (`--ref` closes resume against the same pinned ref).
- [ ] Bounded by `verify.auto_resume_max` (default 2, 0 disables; config-registry regenerated); attempts beyond the bound surface the existing failure with an attempts-count message (tested).
- [ ] Progress condition: a resumption dispatches only when the prior attempt strictly increased the cache-credited PASS count; unit tests cover (a) increasing count → resumes; (b) unchanged count → stops early with the failure surfaced, no further LLM run; (c) progress then stall → exactly one extra attempt.
- [ ] Resumption trail recorded per attempt (attempt number, cache-credited count, remaining count) and visible on the ticket or in the close output (tested).
- [ ] The loop sits at the shared gate seam: an MCP-or-library-path close exercises it in a test, not only the CLI path.
- [ ] Child idea ticket for frontier handoff created + linked discovered_from this ticket before this ticket closes.
- [ ] `make lint` / `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
